subject: microbiology
title: NK Cells, Macrophages, Dendritic Cells and Toll-Like Receptors

steps.tx: **NK cells** are innate lymphocytes that kill without prior sensitisation by balancing activating receptors against inhibitory receptors reading MHC class I (missing self: virus infected and tumour cells that hide class I from CD8 become NK targets). They secrete interferon gamma early and mediate antibody dependent cellular cytotoxicity through CD16 Fc receptors.
steps.say: Hide class I from T cells and NK cells notice the empty chair.

left.title: NK recognition
points: Inhibitory KIRs read self MHC class I

steps.tx: **NK cells** are innate lymphocytes that kill without needing a prior sensitising exposure. Activating receptors push toward killing, while inhibitory receptors read MHC class I and hold the cell back. Virus infected cells and some tumour cells hide class I to escape CD8 T cells, and that missing self removes the inhibitory signal, so they become NK targets. Early in infection these cells release interferon gamma. Through CD16, an Fc receptor, they also kill antibody coated targets, which is antibody dependent cellular cytotoxicity.
steps.say: NK cells kill without prior sensitisation. Inhibitory receptors see MHC class I and spare the cell. Activating receptors push the other way. Virus infected and tumour cells that hide class I from CD8 T cells become missing self targets. NK cells also release interferon gamma early and kill antibody coated cells through CD16.

vis.alt: A diagram shows a natural killer cell sparing a target that displays MHC class I and killing a cell that has lost class I.
vis.caption: Inhibitory receptors read MHC class I as a stay signal, so a cell that hides class I loses protection and is killed. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Macrophages** patrol tissues under local names (Kupffer in liver, alveolar in lung, microglia in brain, splenic and node residents), phagocytose and present antigen, secrete the cytokine weather (TNF, IL 1, IL 6, IL 12), and polarise functionally (classically activated microbicidal versus alternatively activated repair programmes, M1 and M2 shorthand). Granulomas are their stalemate architecture around indigestible organisms.
steps.say: One cell, many addresses: macrophage names change by organ, duties do not.

left.title: Macrophage duties
points: Antigen presentation to effector T cells

right.title: Activation portraits
points: Intracellular pathogens live inside despite it (TB, Salmonella)

steps.tx: **Dendritic cells** sample tissue antigen as immature sentinels, mature on pattern receptor alarm, migrate to nodes, and present with costimulation that alone can prime naive T cells; subsets divide labour (conventional for priming, plasmacytoid secreting type I interferon torrents in viral infection, Langerhans in skin, follicular dendritic unrelated lineage holding antigen for B cells).
steps.say: Immature dendritic cells eat, alarmed ones travel and teach; maturity changes their profession.

left.title: Dendritic journey
points: PAMP alarm induces maturation and migration

right.title: Subset cast
points: Conventional cDC1 cross presentation to CD8

steps.tx: **Toll like receptors** (ten human TLRs) patrol surface and endosomes as the pattern readers named in the innate lesson: TLR4 LPS with MD2 and CD14, TLR2 heterodimers for bacterial lipoproteins, TLR5 flagellin, TLR3 double stranded RNA, TLR7 and 8 single stranded RNA, TLR9 CpG DNA, signalling through MyD88 and TRIF to NF kappa B and interferon factors. Human defects map them clinically (TLR3 herpes encephalitis).
steps.say: Ten readers, two adaptor roads, one inflammatory script with interferon variations.

right.title: Endosomal readers
points: Location suits viral nucleic acid surveillance

steps.tx: **Toll like receptors**, ten of them in humans, read microbial patterns from the cell surface and from endosomes. TLR4 with MD2 and CD14 reads lipopolysaccharide, TLR2 heterodimers read lipoproteins, and TLR5 reads flagellin. TLR3 reads double stranded RNA, TLR7 and TLR8 read single stranded RNA, and TLR9 reads CpG DNA. MyD88 and TRIF carry signals toward NF kappa B and interferon factors. TLR3 deficiency presenting as herpes encephalitis shows that a single reader can have a clinical address.
steps.say: Humans have ten Toll like receptors. Surface TLR4, with MD2 and CD14, reads lipopolysaccharide. TLR2 reads lipoproteins and TLR5 flagellin. Endosomal TLR3, TLR7, TLR8, and TLR9 read double stranded RNA, single stranded RNA, and CpG DNA. MyD88 and TRIF lead to inflammatory and interferon signals. TLR3 defects are linked to herpes encephalitis.

vis.alt: A cell map places Toll like receptors on the surface and inside endosomes, each paired with its microbial ligand.
vis.caption: Surface receptors read bacterial lipopolysaccharide, lipoproteins, and flagellin, while endosomal receptors read viral and bacterial nucleic acids. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Neutrophils** remain innate immunity's infantry: first arrival by chemotaxis (C5a, IL 8, bacterial peptides), phagocytosis and killing by burst, granules and extracellular traps (NETs of DNA and enzyme that snare bacteria while injuring tissue), short lived and pus forming. Their absence or dysfunction writes the infectious tempo of chemotherapy and immunodeficiency alike.
steps.say: Neutrophils arrive first, burn brightly, die as pus, and sometimes throw their DNA as nets.

right.title: Neutrophil failures
points: Left shift and toxic granulation as response signs

steps.tx: **Complement** first contact belongs in this lesson's innate cast: alternative pathway ticks over on microbial surfaces without antibody, lectin pathway reads mannose patterns, opsonising with C3b and summoning neutrophils with C5a before any antibody exists. The immunoglobulin module will run its full cascade; here it earns innate membership honestly.
steps.say: Complement patrols before antibodies exist; antibody only accelerates an old system.

steps.tx: **Interferons type I** (alpha and beta) are innate antiviral cytokines secreted by infected and plasmacytoid cells, inducing antiviral states in neighbours (enzyme systems degrading viral nucleic acid), upregulating MHC class I, and activating NK cells; their therapeutic ghosts persist from the hepatitis era into myeloproliferative niches. Defects present as severe viral disease in otherwise well children.
steps.say: Interferon warns the neighbourhood before the virus arrives; NK cells hear it too.

steps.tx: **Innate lymphoid cells** (ILC1, 2 and 3) mirror helper T cytokine programmes without receptors or memory (interferon gamma, IL 5 and 13, IL 17 and 22 at barriers), completing an innate cast whose every member now has a named defect, drug or diagnostic. Examinations sample representatives per family rather than the whole roll call.
steps.say: Helper programmes without receptors: ILCs are the innate mirror of the helper cast.

left.title: ILC mirror
points: ILC2: IL 5, IL 13, helminths and allergy
ILC3: IL 17, IL 22, mucosal fungi and bacteria
